rheinturmuhr.name: Rheinturm
rheinturmuhr.slogan: A tower that tells the time in lights above the Rhine.
rheinturmuhr.line: The city of Düsseldorf is very beautiful, and if you think of it from afar and happen to have been born there, you feel strangely moved.
rheinturmuhr.by: Heinrich Heine, Ideen. Das Buch Le Grand, 1827

schwebebahn.name: Wuppertal Schwebebahn
schwebebahn.slogan: A train that hangs from the sky and skims the river.
schwebebahn.line: In 1950 a circus baby elephant was put on board as a stunt, panicked, and fell into the Wupper; she was named Tuffi afterwards.

gehrybauten.name: Gehry Buildings
gehrybauten.slogan: Three crooked towers that sway in the Medienhafen light.
gehrybauten.line: Frank Gehry's Neuer Zollhof, finished in 1998, wraps white plaster, red brick and stainless steel into three separate bending buildings.

muengstenerbruecke.name: Müngsten Bridge
muengstenerbruecke.slogan: An iron arch that leaps the Wupper valley.
muengstenerbruecke.line: Opened on 15 July 1897, it rises 107 metres and is the highest railway bridge in Germany.

schlossbenrath.name: Benrath Palace
schlossbenrath.slogan: A pink pleasure palace with its own mirror pond.
schlossbenrath.line: Nicolas de Pigage built it between 1755 and 1770 for Elector Charles Theodor as a pleasure palace, not a seat of government.
